channel_name: This Week in Startups · Jason Calacanis
video_title: Anthropic’s Record IPO, Apple’s Secret AI Agent, Waymo BANNED
gist: Jason Calacanis frames Anthropic's record $81.3B NASDAQ IPO (ticker ANT, $33.2B nine-month revenue) and a crashed tech market with record-low P/Es as a generational buying moment, premised on AI usage growing 100-1,000x from today's ~1% heavy adoption, while selling Bitcoin. He predicts Apple will own a top-three AI agent within 24 months via local models, and warns that California's Waymo freeway ban and proposed AI shutdown powers show political backlash is the key risk to AI and autonomy.

themes.theme: Anthropic IPO: deal terms, governance and pricing discipline

insights.claim: Anthropic listed on NASDAQ under ticker ANT, upsizing to 980 million shares from 825 million to raise $81.3 billion (the largest IPO ever); it opened at $111.50, 34% above the IPO price, peaked near $115, then traded back toward about $83.
insights.speaker: Lon (co-host)
insights.so_what: Post-debut fade toward the offer price signals no easy first-day pop; watch ANT support near the IPO price.

insights.claim: Anthropic reported $33.2 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, versus roughly $2.5 billion a year earlier.
insights.speaker: Lon (co-host)
insights.so_what: Over 10x YoY revenue growth makes ANT a direct read on enterprise AI demand; benchmark peers against this trajectory.
insights.quote: the company reports 33.2 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, up from just about 2.5 billion a year prior

insights.claim: Anthropic's voting control sits in a single class F share held by an LLC of the seven co-founders carrying a fixed 50.1% of votes on general stockholder matters, so public shareholders get little governance say.
insights.speaker: Lon (co-host)
insights.so_what: Governance-sensitive funds/index rules may limit ownership; retail holders are economically exposed without control.

insights.claim: Calacanis defends founder super-voting structures at Anthropic, arguing founder-led companies do better and that Meta and Google shareholders made fortunes by letting founders keep control; investors who object should simply not buy.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Treat dual-class governance as a non-issue for return potential in the view of founder-friendly investors.
insights.quote: If you don't like Zuckerberg and his controlling uh super voting shares or you don't like the ant team and their super controllers, don't buy the stock. Period.

insights.claim: Mega-IPOs are now priced to perfection or even overpriced rather than underpriced for a pop, so buying with a market order on day one tends to get punished; waiting a week or two is preferable.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Use limit orders and wait out initial volatility on large tech IPOs (ANT, a future OpenAI listing).
insights.quote: IPOs is a is a is a science now. It's not alchemy. They don't underpric them and get a pop.

insights.claim: Anthropic's disclosures reveal that a large share of its revenue comes from overages and consumption-based usage rather than subscriptions, giving the market a measurable window into how enterprises spend on AI.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Consumption-weighted revenue scales with token usage, making ANT a leveraged bet on usage growth; track the mix quarterly.

insights.claim: Once OpenAI also goes public, combined with Nvidia, Google and Meta disclosures, investors will have near-full visibility into the health of the AI economy, like seeing all the cards in a poker hand.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: An OpenAI IPO is a key catalyst for resolving AI-bubble uncertainty; watch its filing data.
insights.quote: Once we get OpenAI's numbers, we're going to have full visibility into the AI economy.

themes.theme: AI usage bull case: 100-1,000x token demand from enterprise adoption

insights.claim: Calacanis estimates only about 1% of Western knowledge workers (roughly 300-400 million people) use AI as intensively as AI-first employees do; even in his own AI-first organization it is about 5 of 20 people (25%).
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: The adoption gap implies large untapped demand for AI tokens and seats.

insights.claim: If 80-90% of knowledge workers reach heavy AI usage (about 80x more heavy users) and per-user tokens and agents double yearly, total AI usage could reach 100-1,000x today's levels, meaning current usage is a tiny fraction of eventual capacity.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Supports the long-duration demand case for compute, model providers and inference infrastructure.
insights.quote: I believe what we're experiencing today is somewhere in a fraction of 130th 1500th 1,000th of the capacity.

insights.claim: The co-host reports AI use rising from roughly 1 hour a day two years ago to 5 hours a year ago to 9-9.5 hours of a 10-hour workday now, with the inflection coming when AI is connected to all apps with full context rather than used as a chatbot.
insights.speaker: Lon (co-host)
insights.so_what: Integration/connectors (context access) are the adoption unlock; favor products that embed AI across workflows.

insights.claim: Calacanis predicts AI agents will lift average revenue per employee in corporate America from $500k-$1M to $3-10 million, so spending a few thousand dollars more per employee on AI subscriptions and tokens is trivially justified against $75-125k salaries.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Enterprise AI spend per seat has ample room to rise; bullish for consumption-based AI vendors.
insights.quote: The efficiency gains are being widely underestimated.

insights.claim: Calacanis believes people are at peak cynicism about AI and are greatly underestimating its revenue and efficiency potential.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Sentiment extremes may mark attractive entry points in AI-exposed equities.
insights.quote: we are at peak cynicism and people just do not understand from first principles how transformative this technology is

insights.claim: With Anthropic's IPO proceeds, a potential $50-100 billion OpenAI raise, and roughly $1 trillion from cash-flowing hyperscalers, Calacanis sees about $1.5 trillion of capital already arranged, enough to complete AI buildouts if usage grows 100-1,000x.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Funding risk for the AI capex cycle is lower than feared for well-capitalized players.

themes.theme: Market crash positioning: catching knives in big tech, selling Bitcoin

insights.claim: Amid a market crash with big tech trading at its lowest P/E ratios since the dot-com era, Calacanis calls it a generational buying opportunity and says he will deploy free cash into SpaceX, Tesla, Uber, Shopify, Google and Anthropic (not yet bought).
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: A prominent VC is signaling contrarian accumulation of beaten-down tech; watch these names for capitulation bottoms.
insights.quote: I am going to catch every knife in the stock market I can.

insights.claim: Calacanis attributes the market crash since Democrats took office after a 'blue tsunami' to policy fears of slower growth and AI regulation, saying 401(k)s are down 30-40%.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Policy/regulatory risk is being priced into AI and tech; regulatory clarity could be a rebound catalyst.

insights.claim: Calacanis cites Nvidia around $130-140 and Uber at $65 as incredible opportunities among legendary companies trading low.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Specific price levels he considers attractive for accumulation.

insights.claim: Calacanis predicts Bitcoin will never see a new all-time high (or only perhaps in 10 years) and will massively trail the Magnificent 7/10; he correctly called a test of the 52-week low near $57K and has sold part of his Bitcoin to rotate into AI companies.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Suggests rotating crypto exposure toward productive AI equities; Bitcoin as hedge only.
insights.quote: I think Bitcoin is not going to see an all-time high ever again.

insights.claim: Neocloud stocks such as CoreWeave, Nebius and Applied Digital are harder to underwrite because of layered debt (loans, bonds) and debt-spiral risk, and they compete against Meta, AWS and Google, which have far stronger balance sheets.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Prefer balance-sheet-rich hyperscalers over leveraged neoclouds in the AI infrastructure trade.
insights.quote: what if they have too much debt and they get caught in some kind of debt spiral?

themes.theme: Apple's computer-use agent and local-model advantage

insights.claim: A Bloomberg-spotted Apple job listing shows Apple building a private AI agent that can operate a Mac (use apps, browse, run commands, write/debug code, multi-step tasks), with launch considered as early as end of 2027, while Apple makes it harder for third-party agents to control Macs.
insights.speaker: Lon (co-host)
insights.so_what: Apple entering computer-use agents could squeeze third-party desktop agent startups.

insights.claim: Calacanis predicts Apple will have one of the top three AI agents in the world within 24 months, arriving last but winning on simplicity, trust and local models, because it sits at the intersection of own silicon/local compute, a personal assistant (Siri) and trusted personal data.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Bullish Apple optionality in agents and local inference; Mac Studio demand from local-model users is a tell.
insights.quote: They will have one of the top three agents in the world within 24 months.

insights.claim: Calacanis argues Apple cannot lock down macOS the way it does iOS because desktop users demand freedom to run any app, so third-party agent restrictions will amount to security checkboxes rather than a walled garden.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Third-party desktop agents likely retain Mac access; mobile remains closed.

insights.claim: Calacanis expects Apple, weak at software, to acquire an agentic AI company, naming Perplexity as a possible target.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Potential M&A catalyst for agentic AI startups.
insights.quote: they'll buy perplexity. They'll buy something, I believe.

insights.claim: CrowdStrike's George Kurtz reportedly keeps two 512GB Mac Studios on his desk to experiment with local models, cited as evidence Apple hardware is becoming the default for local AI.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: High-memory Mac sales may be a leading indicator of local-model adoption.

themes.theme: Regulatory backlash: Waymo freeway ban and California AI shutdown powers

insights.claim: California's DMV barred Waymo's driverless cars from state freeways as an 'imminent hazard,' citing entries into construction zones and a car trying to pass police slowing traffic; Waymo paused freeway rides in all markets including Phoenix, Austin and Miami, and must prove corrective action to lift the ban.
insights.speaker: Lon (co-host)
insights.so_what: Burden-of-proof shift to the operator signals the end of self-certification; slows robotaxi scaling timelines.

insights.claim: Calacanis calls the Waymo ban an underreaction and argues robotaxis should stay under 45 mph or carry safety drivers, because one high-speed fatality would be politically weaponized alongside job-loss and wealth-disparity narratives and could shut down the whole industry.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Headline-risk asymmetry for autonomy stocks; a single fatal incident could trigger industry-wide bans.
insights.quote: Slow and steady wins the race. These things should not go above 45 miles an hour.

insights.claim: Calacanis, invested in over a dozen autonomy companies including Tesla, Zipline, Uber and Autolane, expects autonomous share of ride-sharing to grow from 1% to 30% with many winners, and cites New York's Airbnb crackdown (family hotel stays at $3,000-5,000 a night) as proof that regulators can shut down a category.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Long-term autonomy bull case intact but regulatory shutdown risk is real; diversify across players.

insights.claim: Governor Newsom's AI panel recommended an emergency shutdown authority for dangerous models, mandatory third-party audits, state safety standards and authority to cap compute used for recursive self-improvement; Governor-elect Xavier Becerra says he will move quickly to codify shutdown authority.
insights.speaker: Lon (co-host)
insights.so_what: State-level model shutdown powers are a new tail risk for AI labs headquartered in California.

insights.claim: Calacanis expects California to pass such AI rules, prompting AI companies to state-hop and even move data centers and models to Singapore, Malaysia, the Middle East and North Africa, and says fear that these laws pass is part of why hedge funds and traders are exiting tech.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Watch for AI lab relocation announcements and offshore data-center buildouts; Trump floated taxing overseas data centers.

insights.claim: Calacanis argues that without populist measures like a $15 federal minimum wage and broader healthcare, the public will express anger through regulation, local data-center bans and wealth taxes, which raises political risk for tech and AI infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Local opposition to data centers is a growing permitting risk for AI capex.
insights.quote: people can go to their local meeting and ban the data center

themes.theme: Generative AI in Hollywood and consumer AI devices

insights.claim: Calacanis argues AI will cut film budgets from about $100 million to $10 million, producing far more content with much smaller teams and a long tail of creators, while AI is just a flavor of CGI audiences accept if the story is great.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Deflationary pressure on production costs favors AI video tools and independent creators over legacy studios' cost bases.
insights.quote: the budgets will go from $100 million back down to 10 because of AI

insights.claim: Plaud has added connectors letting its recording pin feed Claude and agent tools directly, and has launched Plaud One earbuds at $229 with a built-in eSIM; Calacanis says the company's revenue is impressive enough that he may seek equity.
insights.speaker: Jason Calacanis
insights.so_what: Signals traction in AI wearables/ambient capture (sponsor context; treat with caution).
